subject: Post-incident attestation & log memo — no evidence of PII export
messages:
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@finovexa.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: security@finovexa.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Suspicious traffic during service degradation — request for scope

Kimberly,

We saw a spike of unusual 429/5xx responses from your API between 2027-01-14 22:05 UTC and 22:17 UTC; our telemetry shows a small number of requests that normally return user-account metadata returned a 502. Given compliance needs, we need to confirm whether any of our customers' PII was accessible or exported during that window.

Can you provide a preliminary scope and an estimated time when you can run the log integrity checks? Our security team is on standby and would appreciate an attestation once you’ve completed analysis.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Gomez
Head of Security, Finovexa
security@finovexa.com

Alex — thanks for flagging and apologies for the disruption. I’ve opened SEC-9142 and assigned the investigation to our on-call incident response team. High-level plan:

- Run targeted log integrity scans (API gateway, inference runtime egress, S3 access logs)
- Verify object hashes and check for any unexpected downstream transfers
- Run sample queries against the anonymized KV cache to ensure no TTL/eviction anomaly returned PII
- Produce a short attestation memo and share artifacts (hash manifest, filtered logs)

We’ll prioritize account_id and email fields per your note. Expect first technical findings by EOD PST today; formal attestation by Monday. I’ll loop in Marissa for the SGX/KV cache checks and Evelyn for retention/audit log exports.

Kimberly Park

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 15:12:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Post-incident attestation & log memo — operational findings

Team — summary of technical validation (attachments included):

What we checked
- API gateway request/response logs (nginx/instrumented proxy) for 2027-01-14T22:00:00Z–22:30:00Z
- Inference runtime outbound telemetry and network flows (TCPdump capture sampled)
- S3 access logs for model artifacts and customer-data buckets in the same timeframe
- KV/prefix cache hit/miss traces and GC/eviction events from runtime metrics
- SIEM alerts correlated against our IDS (no lateral movement indicators)

Findings (brief)
- The root cause was a brief autoscaling race condition: two worker pools overlapped during a node restart, producing elevated 502/429 responses. No unauthorized processes or unknown egress destinations were found.
- S3 access logs: all PUT/GET operations in scope were initiated by known service principals; no public ACL changes detected.
- Hash verification: we computed SHA256 hashes of the archived request logs and compared them to the copy retained in our cold archive. Manifest attached: s3-access-hash-manifest.txt — all hashes match.
- KV cache sampling: sampled keys that map to Finovexa account_ids were inspected; returned values are ephemeral runtime artifacts (model context pointers) and do not include customer PII fields (email, ssn, payment info).

Conclusion
- No evidence of data exfiltration or unauthorized access to Finovexa customer PII in the reviewed window.
- Evidence artifacts: log-scan-report-20270118.pdf, s3-access-hash-manifest.txt, and a redacted runtime trace. These are attached for your audit team.

Next steps / recommendations
- We recommend validating your end (any cached client-side telemetry) and confirming you do not have corresponding anomalies.
- We’ll follow up with a short postmortem focused on the autoscaling fix and an ETA for a permanent guardrail (patch scheduled for 2027-01-21).

Marissa Cole
Engineering Lead, Runtime Reliability
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments referenced: log-scan-report-20270118.pdf (redacted logs and summary), s3-access-hash-manifest.txt (sha256 manifest), redwood_root_cause_notes.txt

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@finovexa.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 17:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Formal attestation: Post-incident data integrity statement for Finovexa

Alex — attaching the log-scan report and manifest shared by engineering. Below is Redwood’s formal attestation for the incident window 2027-01-14T22:05:00Z–2027-01-14T22:17:00Z.

Attestation (executive summary)
- Redwood Inference performed a comprehensive integrity check of production artifacts related to the incident and reviewed relevant telemetry, network flows, and object store access logs.
- The checks included SHA256 verification of archived logs against cold storage, sampling of KV/prefix cache entries, and correlation of SIEM/IDS alerts.
- Based on the review, Redwood has found no evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized access, or leakage of Finovexa customer PII during the specified window.

Scope and limitations
- This attestation covers the systems and artifacts under Redwood’s control (API gateway, inference runtime, S3 buckets containing operational logs and model artifacts, and internal cache traces). It does not include any telemetry or storage exclusively controlled by Finovexa.

Artifacts provided
- log-scan-report-20270118.pdf — redacted findings and timeline
- s3-access-hash-manifest.txt — SHA256 manifest used for binary verification
- redwood_root_cause_notes.txt — engineer notes and the planned remediation timeline

We’re available to join a call with your security and compliance teams to walk through the attestation and the artifacts. Please let me know preferred timing; we can also provide a signed attestation letter on company letterhead if required for your audit.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
